question:
A previously healthy 5-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department because of abdominal pain and vomiting for 6 hours. His mother immediately brought him after noticing that he had gotten into the medicine cabinet. The mother is 5 months' pregnant. He appears uncomfortable. His temperature is 37.2°C (99°F), pulse is 133/min and blood pressure is 80/50 mm Hg. Examination shows diffuse abdominal tenderness; there is no guarding or rigidity. Digital rectal examination shows dark-colored stools. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 13.2 g/dL
Leukocyte count 14,100/mm3
Serum
Na+ 136 mEq/L
K+ 3.3 mEq/L
Cl- 105 mEq/L
Urea nitrogen 26 mg/dL
Glucose 98 mg/dL
Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL
Arterial blood gas analysis on room air shows:
pH 7.31
pCO2 32 mm Hg
HCO3- 16 mEq/L
Intravenous fluids are administered. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Ingestion of toxic substance -> Abdominal pain and vomiting -> Dark-colored stools on rectal examination -> Possible gastrointestinal bleeding -> 70%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation with abdominal pain, vomiting, and dark-colored stools suggests possible gastrointestinal bleeding. The most appropriate next step in management is to administer activated charcoal to help absorb any remaining toxic substance in the gastrointestinal tract.
analysis: The patient's presentation with abdominal pain, vomiting, and dark-colored stools raises concern for possible gastrointestinal bleeding. Given the history of accessing the medicine cabinet and the need to absorb any remaining toxic substance, activated charcoal is the most appropriate next step in management. Activated charcoal can help bind to the toxic substance in the gastrointestinal tract and prevent further absorption. This aligns with the standard approach to managing potential toxic ingestions.
